\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Discrete Approximation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.DiscreteApproximation
\section{Overview}
Lipschitz derivative bounds give quadratic linearization estimates. Applied to normalized Boolean blocks, these estimates compare discrete half-differences with partial derivatives and quantify the vanishing approximation error.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic linearization remainder]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_linearization_remainder_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and let $f\colon E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable
at every point, with derivative $D(x)\colon E\to\mathbb R$ at $x$. Suppose $D$ is
Lipschitz in operator norm with constant $C\geq0$. Then, for all $x,y\in E$,
$\|f(y)-f(x)-D(x)(y-x)\|\leq C\|y-x\|^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Half-increment derivative error bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_half_increment_sub_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_linearization_remainder_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space and let $f:E\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable
everywhere, with derivative $Df(x):E\to\mathbb R$. Suppose the derivative map is
$C$-Lipschitz in operator norm for some $C\ge0$. For all $x,v\in E$ and $h\in\mathbb R$,
\[\left|\frac{f(x+hv)-f(x)}{2}-\frac{h}{2}Df(x)[v]\right|\le \frac{C}{2}h^2\|v\|^2.\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Updating a normalized Boolean block]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolBlocks_update}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let
$x\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, choose a
row $i$, a column $j$, and a Boolean value $b$. Encode each Boolean by
$\sigma(\mathrm{false})=1$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{true})=-1$, and define
$S(x)_k=(\sum_{l=1}^m\sigma(x_{kl}))/\sqrt m$, with real division interpreted in the
usual way, including when $m=0$. If $x'$ is obtained by replacing the entry $x_{ij}$ by
$b$, then $S(x')=S(x)+\frac{\sigma(b)-\sigma(x_{ij})}{\sqrt m}e_i$, where $e_i$ is the
vector equal to $1$ in coordinate $i$ and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Block half-difference approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_normalizedBoolBlocks_half_difference_sub_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_half_increment_sub_derivative_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedBoolBlocks_update, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,m\ge0$, let $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative $D(z)$ at every
$z\in\mathbb R^n$, and suppose the map $D\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathcal L(\mathbb
R^n,\mathbb R)$ is $C$-Lipschitz for some $C\ge0$. For a Boolean array
$x=(x_{kl})_{k<n,\,l<m}$ and indices $i<n$, $j<m$, encode false by $1$ and true by $-1$,
and write $S(x)_k=m^{-1/2}\sum_{l<m}\sigma(x_{kl})$. If $x^{0}$ and $x^{1}$ are obtained
by setting entry $(i,j)$ to false and true, respectively, then
\[\left|\frac{f(S(x^{0}))-f(S(x^{1}))}{2}-\frac{D(S(x))e_i}{\sqrt m}\right|\le\frac{2C}{m},\]
where $e_i$ is the $i$th coordinate vector.
\end{lemma}
